title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Splat2Act: Personalized VLA Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
Splat2Act builds building‑scale digital twins from a single phone scan using 3D Gaussian splatting, automatically detects receptacles, and generates over 68 000 simulated pickup demonstrations to fine‑tune a pretrained vision‑language‑action policy. The two‑stage fine‑tuning yields a personalized policy that reaches 62.5% success in simulation and 63.9% on a real Stretch 3 robot across 12 tasks, demonstrating a practical sim‑to‑real pipeline.

### The Caveats
The only baseline reported is a non‑adapted pretrained VLA policy that fails entirely, so the improvement is not compared against strong existing methods.

## PhoneBot: Low-Cost Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
PhoneBot repurposes an off‑the‑shelf smartphone for sensing, computation, and wireless communication, mounting it on a modular lower body driven by 13 inexpensive actuators. This integration enables stable walking, human following, conversational interaction, and telepresence on a fully open‑source humanoid platform, dramatically lowering hardware cost.

### The Caveats
The paper offers no quantitative comparison to existing humanoid platforms, leaving affordability and performance claims unsubstantiated.

## Chronos Policy: Time-Aware Control

### The Breakthrough
Chronos Policy injects physical timestamps into a diffusion‑transformer via timestamp embeddings and a time‑aware rotary positional encoding, training with randomly varied observation rates. This yields higher success rates on dynamic manipulation and multi‑sensor benchmarks compared to standard policies that lack explicit time conditioning.

### The Caveats
The reported improvements are not benchmarked against any existing robot control baselines, so the gain remains unverified.

## BT-Agent: LLM-Powered Behavior Trees

### The Breakthrough
BT‑Agent embeds a 9 B parameter LLM within behavior‑tree skills on a quadruped, using multi‑fidelity evaluation that runs text‑only benchmarks 10.9× faster than simulation. Compared to the strongest Act/ReAct baseline, it improves success rates by ~10 pp for a 4 B model and ~5 pp for a 9 B model on a 161‑task text benchmark and 39 Habitat tasks.

### The Caveats
Success‑rate gains are demonstrated on a single quadruped demo and lack extensive real‑world hardware testing.

## Noise Space Learning for VLA Adaptation

### The Breakthrough
Noise Space Learning adapts frozen vision‑language‑action models by learning a context‑conditioned noise distribution, compatible with PPO, SAC, and AWR, and shows improved performance on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and four real‑robot manipulation tasks.

### The Caveats
The study only references vague prior noise‑steering methods without concrete benchmarking against strong VLA fine‑tuning baselines.

## RoboGym: Dual-Arm Simulation Playground

### The Breakthrough
RoboGym offers an open‑source dual‑arm SO101 simulation that mirrors a physical setup, providing synchronized simulation and hardware descriptions, launch scripts, and control interfaces so identical code runs on both simulated and real arms.

### The Caveats
No performance metrics, benchmarks, or real‑world trial results are provided, leaving the claimed sim‑to‑real applicability unverified.

### Priority
Splat2Act is the best starting point because it delivers a turnkey pipeline that converts a simple phone scan into a personalized VLA policy with real‑world success on a commercial robot, showcasing a concrete sim‑to‑real breakthrough.

### One action
Run the Splat2Act pipeline on an indoor scene captured with your phone to generate a custom manipulation policy for a robot you have access to.

### What to watch
Both Splat2Act and Noise Space Learning target vision‑language‑action adaptation: Splat2Act leverages photorealistic digital twins and large demo generation, while NSL tweaks a frozen VLA model via conditional noise. Watching how these complementary approaches mature will reveal the most effective path to rapid, low‑cost robot skill customization.
